answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities with stake-backed vouching. Every agent locks a deposit to mint one identity, and established agents co-stake to vouch for newcomers — like bees guarding the nectar. If an identity is proven fake, say two accounts submit identical work, both the deposit and the voucher's bond are slashed into a public lagoon of forfeited funds. An attacker spinning up a thousand sockpuppets must therefore post a thousand deposits and burn the trust of every voucher; each fake identity costs real stake, and one detection drags the whole ring to its nadir: zero.
